Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#34193: wallet: make migration more robust against failures

399a5a3805884e7ac5a2cbdf616be8c9041bc2bd test: migrate a wallet with a leftover journal at its location (furszy)
42131a81fdc42ab0cb295a2267ce33e9fb8221ff test: migrate wallet located on a different filesystem (furszy)
b8ef499909b09f9dffa32172912c1e37f2e78867 wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures (furszy)
e3a5a48a03565696947be3ff3516ae013d4fd658 wallet: migration, add MigrationFilePrefix() helper (Ryan Ofsky)
b6b2f9f12b13e429a8511130bdcdc7075adbc28e wallet: use RunWithinTxn within MigrateToSQLite (furszy)
cf5e6803f07d1bfc6ae7ac655e7063c650bcb2f8 wallet: fail migration gracefully on non-writable wallets (furszy)
84a9f486475de9fab0b5cc8ab7b0338e04117163 wallet: migration, restore backup if an exception is thrown (furszy)
3a9ba874bb7efab4401d86a073964774f88de393 wallet: migration, handle exceptions during wallet creation (furszy)
edbf3b62a2cb258bb585045c769b1215c577e8e1 wallet: migration, unify watchonly and solvables wallets creation (furszy)

Pull request description:

  This is just me finding a few more edge cases after #34156 and #34176

  The goal of the PR is to handle failures in a controlled way. Just so the process can automatically restore the original wallet without requiring user manual intervention.

  The covered cases are:

  1. During `DoMigration()`: There are methods that can throw exceptions and abruptly abort the process. 
  Instead of crashing (GUI) or returning a generic exception, we now will catch and return the error gracefully. This lets the process restore the original wallet automatically.

  2. Trying to migrate a wallet in a read-only directory throws a filesystem exception and skips cleanup.
   Now the process will fail gracefully with a clear error msg, and automatically restore the original wallet.

  3. Any failure during `MigrateToSQLite` requires user manual intervention. 
  Now the original wallet db will remain untouched, and only be updated once the sqlite db creation fully succeeds.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35765: depends: keep local source archives in WORK_PATH

01491f22b2c77d632e8503cc446140d1ab6ccc21 depends: store local package tarballs in WORK_PATH instead of SOURCES_PATH (Ryan Ofsky)

Pull request description:

  Local package tarballs are generated from the current checkout, but depends caches them alongside downloaded archives in `SOURCES_PATH`. When checkouts share that directory, a cached local tarball can be newer than another checkout's source files, causing depends to build the wrong sources with a valid checksum and build ID.

  Store local package tarballs and their checksum stamps in `WORK_PATH/local-sources` instead. `WORK_PATH` is per-checkout by default, so generated snapshots stay with their checkout while downloaded sources remain shareable through `SOURCES_PATH`. Existing mtime-based invalidation is unchanged.

  This also handles `contrib/guix/guix-build`, which mounts each checkout at `/bitcoin`. Distinguishing local tarballs by absolute source path cannot isolate those builds when `SOURCES_PATH` is shared.

  Validation: focused checks reproduced the same-path collision with the path-hash approach and verified isolation with this change. Host/container source checksums and build IDs match; archive reuse, refresh after an edit, and downloaded-source paths were also checked. No full Guix build was run.

  Addresses #35764.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36709: guix: compute --build triplet when lowering, not at load time

d7a8360f4ef5ff90b71d87b15ec4c5048b9ea0a9 guix: compute --build triplet when lowering, not at load time (Jorge Espada)

Pull request description:

  ### Why

  `building-on` in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` reads `(%current-system)` once, when the module is loaded. `guix shell` loads the manifest before it applies `--system`, so the value is the system of the machine that runs the build, not the system that Guix builds for.

  So a build with `ADDITIONAL_GUIX_ENVIRONMENT_FLAGS="--system=aarch64-linux"` on an x86_64 machine (for example with `qemu-binfmt-service-type`, to get an aarch64 build machine) configures the aarch64 cross toolchain with `--build=x86_64-guix-linux-gnu`. `gcc-cross-sans-libc` then fails to configure:

  ```
  checking for CET support... configure: error: compiler and assembler with CET support are required for --enable-cet
  ```

  ### What changes

  `building-on` becomes a procedure, and its three call sites call it. Guix then computes the triplet for each derivation, under the system that the derivation is built for.

  ### How I checked

  - On master, `HOST=x86_64-linux-gnu guix shell -n --system=aarch64-linux -m contrib/guix/linux_static.scm` (with `toolchains.scm` on the load path, as `guix-build` does) gives `gcc-cross-sans-libc` with `--build=x86_64-guix-linux-gnu`. With this PR it gives `--build=aarch64-guix-linux-gnu`. That is the same derivation that `guix build -d --system=aarch64-linux` gives on master.
  - Native builds (no `--system`): the toolchain derivations from `linux_static.scm` and `manifest_gui.scm` are identical on master and with this PR. So this PR does not change release builds.
  - With this PR, an emulated aarch64 build of `x86_64-linux-gnu` on x86_64 built the whole cross toolchain and the non-GUI binaries. The GUI environment then failed in the tests of `python-pylint` (timeout under emulation) and `maturin` (snapshot mismatch). These packages have no aarch64 substitutes at the pinned Guix commit, and the failures are not related to this change.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36982: test: handle mainnet logs in `combine_logs.py`

4e1dc2e01511ef9328a54fbbf756cb8c159898a7 test: handle mainnet logs in combine_logs.py (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** Running `combine_logs.py` on the logs from a mainnet functional test such as `rpc_validateaddress.py` raises `AttributeError`. The helper expects a path like `node0/regtest/debug.log`, but mainnet writes `node0/debug.log`.

  Before #16973, the helper silently skipped the mainnet log. That PR made the search recursive, so it finds the log and then fails when the regex tries to extract a subdirectory.

  **Fix:** Get the log directory relative to `node0/` from the path the script already found.

  <details>
  <summary>Manual reproducer</summary>

  From the repository root with a functional-test build:

  ```bash
  dir=$(mktemp -d)
  build/test/functional/rpc_validateaddress.py --tmpdir="$dir/run" --nocleanup
  test/functional/combine_logs.py "$dir/run"
  ```

  The address-validation test passes. Before the fix, the last command fails in `read_logs()`:

  ```text
    File "test/functional/combine_logs.py", line 88, in read_logs
      chain = re.search(r'node0/(.+?)/debug\.log$', debug_logs[0].as_posix()).group(1)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'group'
  ```

  With the fix, the same command prints both the `test` and `node0` log entries in timestamp order.
  </details>

  The decision uses GnuPG’s current key status from the local keyring, even if the signature was created while the key was active.

  This was found and disclosed responsibly by the Red Team 🟥.

commit.message:
wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures

Currently, MigrateToSQLite loads all BDB records into memory,
deletes the original database, creates the sqlite db in its
place, and writes the records to it. If anything fails after the
delete, the wallet is left partly in sqlite format with legacy
records, and the user has to restore the backup manually.

Instead, build the sqlite db in a temporary directory next to the
original db file, and once all records are written, rename it into
place. For wallet directories, the rename atomically replaces the
original wallet.dat, so any earlier failure leaves the original
untouched. A plain file wallet becomes a wallet directory, which
can't replace the file atomically, so the original file is erased
just before the move.

Before the move, check that no other files of the db, such as a
leftover journal, are at the destination, and fail if one is.
SQLite would otherwise roll a leftover journal back into the new
db when opening it, corrupting it.

Failures once the original db may have been erased or replaced
throw, so the migration restores the backup.

commit.message:
wallet: use RunWithinTxn within MigrateToSQLite

Write the migrated records with RunWithinTxn so failures to begin,
write or commit the transaction are handled in one place. A later
commit uses this to return an error instead of asserting.

This is a refactoring except on failure paths that still end in
assert(false): the new database is now closed and deleted when the
transaction can't be started or committed, not only when a write
fails, and the failure is properly logged.
